3. Throughout the 1978-1981 HAP, more detailed date will be available relating to the delivery of housing assistance in San Jose. Additionally, the housing assistance delivered is compared with past goals and influenced the establishment of future goals to achieve a distribution of assistance that proportionally addresses the needs of the elderly and handicapped and large family households.
4. According to proposed HUD regulations, the 1978-1981 HAP sets a goal of resolving San Jose's identified housing assistance needs within 20 years. In order to accomplish that goal, annual goals of 1859 additional assisted units are proposed (1812 per year would actually achieve the goal).
5. The "General Locations" portion of the "Three Year Housing Program" was altered to assist developers in locating new projects. Last year's plan designated some areas that were "marginally approvable". The plan explained the criteria that would be used to determine whether or not a site would be approvable in a "marginal" census tract. However, this system led to confusion on the part of developers. This year, based on the percentages of lower-income and ethnic minority households and subsidized rental units in each census tract, a definite designation was made as to the approvability of additional housing assistance.
C. SPECIFIC ELEMENTS OF CDBG PROGRAM
The proposed plan for the 1978-1981 Community Development Block Grant program continues the basic strategy followed during the previous three-year program - the provision of comprehensive neighborhood revitalization efforts in designated target areas. The current proposal intensifies and geographically expands all but one of the previous target neighborhoods, adds two new neighborhoods, and provides for several projects not tied to specific areas.
